notes.title: T-money
notes.text: One transit card (T-money, 티머니) works on Seoul's subways, buses and many taxis. Tap in and tap out: transfers between subway and bus within 30 minutes are mostly free.

notes.title: Subway seats
notes.text: The seats at the ends of each car (노약자석) are for elderly, pregnant and disabled passengers. Pink seats are for pregnant women. Even when they're empty, young people usually leave them free.

notes.title: 빨리 빨리
notes.text: Seoul moves fast — 빨리 빨리 ("quick, quick") is a famous Korean saying. Subway trains come every few minutes, and many stations have screens showing exactly when the next train arrives.

notes.title: Gyeongbokgung
notes.text: Built in 1395, Gyeongbokgung (경복궁) was the main royal palace of the Joseon dynasty. Visitors wearing hanbok get in free, which is why you'll see so many people in rented hanbok around the palace.

notes.title: Coming and going
notes.text: Leaving home: 다녀오겠습니다 ("I'll go and come back"). Coming home: 다녀왔습니다 ("I went and came back"). Whoever is home answers: 다녀왔어요? or 왔어?
